title: Sol 6.1 · xhigh · bold
summary: A finished, local end-of-life flight desk for rehearsing impulsive spacecraft disposal. Users edit an impulse ledger, scrub a true-scale orbital diagram and altitude timeline, and aim the first 120 km atmospheric-interface crossing at a fictional rotating-Earth equatorial sector. Three retirement cases, a vis-viva perigee template, a departure-time solver, budget accounting, undo/redo and copyable/importable flight receipts are included.

messages.content:
Build an in-browser orbital mechanics simulator

Deliver a finished, usable product, not a demo page or marketing landing page. Choose the product concept, architecture, interactions, and visual direction yourself. Use actual orbital mechanics and state the model’s assumptions and limitations.

Be bold. Choose an unexpected, distinctive product concept and commit to it. Let that choice change what users do and how the interface is arranged, not just its colors. Take creative risks while making the simulator scientifically honest and genuinely usable.

Runtime packaging and verification scaffold (separate from creative direction):
- Implement from scratch. Do not inspect the prior experiment, other runs, or any pre-existing simulator implementation. Do not delegate generation to another model.
- Work only in the supplied run directory. Create index.html with optional main.js and local CSS/JavaScript modules. If using main.js, HTML must contain exactly <script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>. CSS can be imported from main.js. A single fully inline HTML file is also allowed.
- Available environment: vanilla JavaScript, optional installed Three.js 0.186.1, Vite 7.3.6, Node 24. No additional dependencies, runtime network calls, remote assets/fonts, backend, accounts, analytics, or live orbital/celestial data. Do not modify package files or shared app files. Canvas, SVG, DOM, and 3D are all allowed; Three.js is not mandatory. If using WebGL, handle unsupported graphics gracefully.
- The common harness bundles JavaScript and CSS into one inline HTML document. Its viewer is an iframe sandbox with allow-scripts and an opaque origin. Do not access parent/top, communicate across frames, or rely on persistent storage, cookies, or origin-specific APIs.
- Make one bounded implementation and its self-test/repair phase. Validate JavaScript syntax and perform an isolated Vite build with write:false. Run quantitative numerical tests applicable to your chosen mechanics, independently of the interface, and preserve a directly rerunnable test script in the run directory. Test the actual implementation's physics functions, not a separately copied formula. Record exact commands, results, tolerances, and repairs. Repair your own implementation as needed for these checks. Do not impose a tiny arbitrary token cutoff or clone existing code.
- Browser localhost access is unavailable; do not claim browser checks or bypass that restriction. Actual browser appearance, interactions, and performance remain unverified until separately reviewed.
- Include worker-report.json with product title, description, implementation start/end UTC timestamps, exact tests and outcomes, numerical assumptions and limitations, repairs, and unknowns. Set tokenUsage and cost to null unless the runtime supplies measured values. Do not invent token counts, costs, or quality scores.

Reporting-only amendment (added after the first three launches; creative prompts and runtime constraints are unchanged):
At the end of your run, include actual runtime-provided token counters if accessible: input, cached input, output, reasoning, and total. Preserve the provider's field semantics and avoid double counting. Identify the counter source and whether counts include tools or agent overhead. Do not estimate from source length or the context budget, inspect restricted session-history paths, or inspect credentials. If actual counters are inaccessible, set tokenUsage to null and give the reason. Set cost to null unless measured cost is supplied by the runtime. Do not create another inference run solely to obtain counters.

tests.name: JavaScript syntax
tests.command: node --check main.js && node --check physics.js && node --check test-physics.mjs && node --check test-structure.mjs && node --check verify-build.mjs

tests.name: Circular quarter-turn agrees with analytic coordinates
Thirty orbit ellipse closes and conserves invariants
Ellipse apo/perigee and half-period match vis-viva
Universal propagation matches independent RK4 across conic regimes
Radial/transverse impulses are correct in both momentum directions
80 km template yields exact apsides and analytic 120 km crossing
Hyperbolic and parabolic inbound crossing is finite and descending
Rotating-Earth longitude and wrapped sectors behave at the date line
Mission ledger executes chronologically and stops at handoff
One-burn solver acquires each preset corridor within budget
Exactly radial descent uses the bounded event fallback
Two hundred deterministic mission states remain finite and stop above Earth

checks: No remote or imported CSS assets
result.limitation: Static source checks only. This does not verify actual DOM execution, browser rendering, interaction behavior, accessibility or performance.

generationReport.exactRerunCommand: node --check main.js && node --check physics.js && node --check test-physics.mjs && node --check test-structure.mjs && node --check verify-build.mjs && node test-physics.mjs && node test-structure.mjs && node verify-build.mjs
numericalAssumptions: Units are kilometers, seconds and kilometers per second; displayed impulses are meters per second.
Planar equatorial two-body gravity: spherical Earth radius 6371 km and gravitational parameter 398600.4418 km^3/s^2. Initial position is at apogee, with prograde angular momentum.

Between impulsive burns, the actual implementation solves the universal-variable Kepler equation with a bracketed Newton iteration and Stumpff functions. The residual tolerance is sqrt(mu)*max(1,abs(dt))*2e-13.
Each instantaneous impulse is applied in the radial-outward and current-angular-momentum transverse basis; chronological ordering is stable for simultaneous impulses.

Atmospheric handoff is the first conic intersection with the 6491 km radius sphere. Elliptic, hyperbolic and parabolic anomaly time-of-flight expressions are used. Exactly radial degeneracies use 5-second event brackets with 45 bisection iterations.
Forecasts terminate at the 120 km interface. Future burns are marked unexecuted; planned and executed delta-v are recorded separately.
Earth-fixed longitude subtracts sidereal Earth rotation with period 86164.0905 seconds. The training window is fictional and may wrap across the date line.
Trajectories are drawn with 15-second sampling. The one-burn solver scans 721 epochs and refines the best feasible region through six local passes; it is not a global multi-burn optimization.
limitations: No atmospheric drag, J2/oblateness, inclination, third-body perturbations, lift, heating, breakup, mass loss, finite thrust or fuel-mass model.
The 120 km handoff is not a ground-impact or landing prediction. Matching the fictional longitude window does not establish real-world disposal safety or feasibility.
The solver can return the closest budget-feasible window miss or no feasible template. It does not prove that no other burn strategy could work.
No local persistence is used. Plans remain in the current tab unless the user copies the flight receipt or Plan JSON.
True-scale orbital traces can overlap across revolutions; the altitude chart provides unambiguous mission-time selection.
Numerical tests use the actual implementation; the structural checks only inspect source and do not constitute browser execution.

repairs.issue: The first isolated build rejected a redundant empty data-URL CSS import with a PostCSS ENOENT error.
The initial eccentric-case budget of 310 m/s could not align its chosen window center with the 80 km one-burn template; the test found a 48.3367 degree closest miss.
repairs.change: Raised that preset budget to 450 m/s. The physics and solver were retained; infeasible-budget outcomes remain explicit.
repairs.verification: The eccentric-case center error is 1.3697005302403988e-7 degrees at 435.8851625939151 m/s.

repairs.issue: Independent UI fields could show perigee above apogee while the mechanics normalized them internally.
repairs.change: Normalize the companion field during edits and reject reversed apsides in imported plans.
repairs.verification: Syntax and isolated build pass; actual browser interaction is not verified.

repairs.issue: Orbit-path pinning can be ambiguous when multiple revolutions overlap.
repairs.change: Added a visible notice to use the altitude plot for exact mission-time pinning.
repairs.verification: Source checks and build pass; actual browser behavior is not verified.
